finding.title: Recovery saves held A material inside independent current B draft
finding.description: recoveryMaterials returns every input.items entry. The attachment input intentionally retains captured A while B is edited, because A must remain explicitly recoverable. App serializes this backing set as B CompleteDraft.attachments. The existing draftItems projection excludes held/inTransit files except files actually in current composer, but Recovery bypasses it. UI B can be correct while its persisted complete draft contains A+B.

causalChain.fact: Capture A before send, rotate settings draft ownership, retain frozen material and A ids in pending; begin Recovery handoff before official send detaches composer.

reconciliationInput deliberately protects held ids from automatic deletion. draftItems already distinguishes current composer attachments from held/inTransit items and preserves non-held unverified selections. capture stores a separate hold without consuming input.

The public composer return observer removes only automatically returned A chips and restores guarded B text. bindComposer receives draftComposer, whose getState masks transient A while capture.returning is active. UI can correctly retain B while A remains in backing input for later explicit restoration.
failed changes submission state but retains value and backing input; successful explicit restoration later discards hold. Retaining A is required, not itself the defect.

Recovery directly reads input.getSnapshot().items and maps all metadata into CompleteDraft; it does not use draftItems or the guarded composer membership. Thus B settings/text are composed with A+B attachments.

While handoff is live, changed defers current snapshot. cancelHandoff clears it and immediately rereads host.draft; enqueue saves that supplied JSON under existing CAS. Journal does not union attachments or select wrong rows; wrong membership was already in the data.

whyExpectationIsCorrect: B is a separately owned current draft after settings.detach. Held A has its own pending/material capture and restore action. Neither a shared backing controller nor matching A/B text grants held A membership in B.

CompleteDraft is the persistent restoration payload, not a display of all recoverable project/view materials. Keeping A+B in that record can restore the wrong files after reload and conflates two draft identities.

The test uses exact id/name/reference order from the real uploaded B item and explicitly confirms current UI B one-file state. Do not loosen to containsB, filter the saved row in the test, erase A, or omit refs from persistence.

heldOnlyFilterReview.basis: Existing draftItems prioritizes actual current composer IDs over held and inTransit, preserves input order and includes unverified selections not yet rendered as chips (attachments.tsx165–179). Held describes recovery ownership, not exclusive absence from current draft.

counterexamples.facts: Explicit restore keeps the hold until after settings.restoreCaptured, setText and each addAttachment. Settings replacement synchronously calls recovery.changed; composer additions synchronously notify draft subscribers. At those moments current A items must be persisted even while held still names A. Unconditional exclusion writes no A during these observations. A later successful onDraftChange repairs the final record, but does not make earlier observed data faithful.

The per-file await is guarded by ownership/generation and current draft checks; if a lease changes or an add fails after a partial mutation, catch reports the error but does not roll back current text/files, and discardFailedSubmission is not reached. A unconditional held filter would persist the visible partial A as no files. No mounted partial-restore failure was run in this review; complete attachment add itself publishes synchronously, so this is not evidence of a long natural network wait.

Old explicit restore sets held text and adds held files but does not discardFailedSubmission afterward. A filter excluding all held IDs would continue omitting explicitly restored current A until the user separately discards the hold. Existing current-ID-first selector deliberately supports this state.

Core failure/cancel returns held files to current attachments before binding records failure. In plain old binding that returned A is a real current member and must not be discarded by held-only filtering. MSG03 differs: guarded draftComposer deliberately exposes B during automatic return; reuse that exact bound read port rather than raw core state.

heldOnlyFilterReview.noBQualification: In MSG03 bindPreparedDraftReturn, even an empty B is preserved and automatic A is removed from the guarded draft; therefore no-B does NOT by itself prove A must be included immediately after cancellation. Include A once genuinely current through explicit restore, and preserve its separate held input meanwhile.
heldOnlyFilterReview.minimumCorrectInterface: A narrow read-only projection on existing ConversationAttachments, using existing draftItems with the exact currently bound composer port; session reads it. Guard lifetime identity on bind/unbind, no second store. A session-only implementation is acceptable only if it can consume this same authoritative current/held/inTransit membership, not a copy of an incomplete held predicate.

release7272Impact.sharedFact: attachments.tsx is byte-identical at 7272 and 61185. Both session.recoveryMaterials expose raw input.items; 7272 App666–668 serializes them. This proves shared projection code, not identical Thread behavior or reproduced production failure.
release7272Impact.differenceThatMatters: MSG03 adds a guarded automatic-return/explicit-complete-draft mechanism and fixture-only await after real adapter.send. Old 7272 Thread has neither that MSG guard nor the new material-cancel button; core return becomes actual current A under the old behavior.

originalAsyncChain.fact: File validation/arrayBuffer/digest/capability/upload waits happen during add/upload before item becomes ready. Original send checks abort and item membership, then synchronously complete(item); async return adds microtask settlement but no network/file wait.

Before official detach/send, captureDraft rejects any unready or missing file and ordered composer mismatch. A natural invalid-file/upload failure therefore does not establish the A-detached/B-editable material-await scenario; it remains an unsent draft validation failure.

Core can await whenSendable and Promise.allSettled and can return a failed submission, but with the current adapter plus ready precondition the inspected normal send path has only microtask completion after ready uploads. No public human-edit task window equivalent to the fixture hold was demonstrated.

A local Outbox/Queue receipt is created synchronously before storage/network dispatch awaits. Thread consumes held A immediately after detecting that receipt. Delaying HTTP ACK is consequently a different boundary and cannot stand in for material preparation.

Fourth-run fixture calls and validates original.send first, then deliberately awaits holdValidated. The cancel arm retains its promise across abort for a later-settlement check. This makes the MSG invariants genuinely exercised, but is an explicit test interleaving absent from the old original adapter.

Old pre-handoff failure returns A if the destination is empty; old core failure/cancel may merge A before current text/files. No new MSG material cancel button exists here. Natural file-validation failure alone does not prove B-only visible state plus hidden A in Recovery.

release7272Impact.boundedConclusion: No ordinary, independently controllable original file-validation/adapter-await path was found that reproduces the fourth-run B-only UI/A+B persisted mismatch on 7272. This is NOT proof that all old failures are safe; reentrant authority changes and other schedules were not executed or exhaustively proven. Do not report old 7272 as runtime-reproduced from same blob, and do not promote 7272 material safety from Release8964 text/receipt evidence.
release7272Impact.releaseRecommendation: If the release promises the repaired current-draft membership boundary, carry the minimal shared projection fix plus its precise existing-session consumer into a new fixed Web source, without waiting for all MSG03 features. Review/validate the old consumer adaptation explicitly; do not copy incomplete App/session held filtering or blindly transplant MSG03 App. Backend 7272 late-logout dependency remains independently required. Until original artifact supply exists, the known 7272 source remains a source candidate rather than an immutable tested release. Whether the old unmodified candidate is acceptable must retain this unproven material boundary, not claim four-App material coverage.
